title: Building words with prefixes and suffixes

blocks.content: Long words are often a small root word with extra parts added. Learn the parts and you can work out the whole word's meaning.
A prefix goes in FRONT of a root word and changes its meaning. 'un-' means 'not', so 'unhappy' means 'not happy'.

steps: Add the prefix un- to the front: 'unkind'.

blocks.question: What does 'un-' mean in the word 'unlock'?
blocks.explain: The prefix un- means 'not' or 'the opposite', so 'unlock' means to undo a lock.
blocks.rule: The prefix un- means 'not' or 'the opposite of'.

blocks.content: A suffix goes at the END of a root word. '-ful' means 'full of', so 'hopeful' means 'full of hope'.

blocks.explain: The suffix -ful means 'full of', so 'careful' means full of care.

blocks.content: A prefix at the front, a suffix at the end, a root in the middle — break a word into parts and its meaning opens up. Let's practise!
